thread:
Sophie (AE): Quick sync — RivetTech wants a POC to move from CompetitorX -> Redwood. Main asks: prompt parity, observed response deltas, pricing delta, and a security questionnaire. Can SE/security weigh in on major blockers?

Ravi (SE): Do we know how they're currently calling CompetitorX? streaming vs non-streaming, function-calling, or custom stop-token handling? those are the usual parity gotchas.

Sophie (AE): They said REST v1/generate endpoints, non-streaming today, but they have a lot of prompt templates and post-processing that assumes competitor tokens/stops.

Gabe (Solutions): Recommend 2-week POC. Scope: 1) compatibility shim that maps their request shape to Redwood API, 2) a test corpus of ~200 prompts for regression checks, 3) side-by-side sampling for top-k/top-p differences. We'll run T=0.7 and deterministic seeds where possible.

Ravi (SE): For the shim, we should preserve these behaviors: stop tokens, max_tokens semantics, role system (if they use role/meta fields), and the exact prefixing they do. Tokenization differences will still cause small deltas — call that out in the report.

Gabe (Solutions): Example mapping snippet to include in runbook:

```
# pseudo-mapping (CompetitorX -> Redwood)
out = redwood.generate(
  model=map_model(comp_model),
  prompt=competitor.payload.prompt,
  max_tokens=competitor.payload.max_tokens,
  stop=competitor.payload.stop_tokens,
  temperature=competitor.payload.temperature
)
```

Gabe (Solutions): We'll also include a normalization step to strip whitespace and canonicalize newlines before diffing outputs — reduces noise.

Ivy (Security): From security side: they asked for SOC2, VPC peering options, KMS integration, data retention options, and an export of audit logs for the POC window. Also need to confirm we can sign their inbound security questionnaire SLA addendum. If they require on-prem/private, flag lead time.

Tom (Sales Eng): Pricing question: they want an apples-to-apples pricing comparison vs CompetitorX. For the POC we can offer a time-limited trial credit + metered hosted usage. If they plan steady traffic we should propose Reserved/Dedicated quote — I can draft ranges.

Ravi (SE): One more technical parity note: CompetitorX does result-filtering hooks in their infra (post-hoc rerank). If RivetTech uses that to remove hallucinations, we'll need to run same reranker or provide a shim. Otherwise perceived quality will vary.

Sophie (AE): Action items: (1) Ravi/Gabe, produce a one-page POC runbook & mapping (+ sample code) by EOD tomorrow, (2) Ivy, list the exact questionnaire items we can auto-answer and items needing legal/ops signoff, (3) Tom, draft a POC pricing blurb and a rough Dedicated quote band. I'll send to RivetTech and ask for the 200-prompt corpus. :thumbsup:

Gabe (Solutions): I'll own the runbook. Will include test harness + instructions to capture their original outputs for side-by-side diffs. Expect initial draft ~18:00 PT tomorrow.

Ivy (Security): I'll compile answers and a short list of 'needs legal' items. Expect by tomorrow morning.

Tom (Sales Eng): I'll draft pricing + note on reserved capacity lead time.

Sophie (AE): Great — if anyone hits a blocker for the POC (eg: they require streaming parity or on-prem), ping me and I'll escalate to AM/AE leadership. Thanks all.
